tagline.text: A tribal festival held every March alongside the town's founding anniversary

location.label: Location
location.text: Municipal plaza and national highway area, T'boli, South Cotabato

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Every March, early to mid month (usually March 5–16)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500~4,000 (transport from General Santos, one night's lodging and meals)

children.text: The Seslong Festival is the signature festival of T'boli in South Cotabato, held every March together with the town's founding anniversary. For about 12 days there are parades, street dancing, concerts, a Tribal Day program and sports competitions, with a pilgrimage to Lake Holon alongside.

The Seslong Festival is held every March in the municipality of T'boli in South Cotabato, in southern Mindanao. T'boli is named after the indigenous T'boli people who live here, and it became a municipality on March 5, 1974 under Presidential Decree No. 407. The festival is therefore built around the founding anniversary, running about twelve days from March 5. The 2017, 2020 and 2023 editions were all listed as March 5–16, which shows this pattern. The municipality has 25 barangays, a population of 105,296 in the 2024 census, and sits on a plateau at about 572 m above sea level, so it is cooler than the lowlands.

Seslong is a T'boli word meaning "marketplace or gathering," and the municipality's official site says it symbolizes the unity of the T'boli and neighboring tribes (a 2016 local news report described it as gathering in one place to exchange goods and enjoy various socio-cultural activities). So it is an occasion when tribal communities come together and share their culture. T'boli is also known for Lake Holon, T'nalak weaving and brass craft, and these aspects of tribal culture are often presented during the festival. However, the program changes each year, so you need to check that year's schedule for what will be held. According to the municipality's tourism information, the town has the T'boli Museum and Cultural Village, the 25-level waterfall Hikong Bente (in Barangay Laconon), the Bakngeb river cave and the dormant volcano Mt. Melibengoy. Lake Holon is a lake in the crater of this mountain.

The 2017 schedule began on the first day with a dawn fun run, an off-road challenge, religious events, a torch parade, an opening concert and fireworks. The following days were filled with local events such as basketball, volleyball and billiards tournaments, a Governor's Night, hip-hop and cheer dance competitions, a medical fair, a shooting competition, a car show and motocross. March 14 was Tribal Day with a concert, and the last day, March 16, had a grand parade, a street dancing competition, a culmination program, a concert and fireworks. It is closer to a local community festival than a program made for tourists, so keep that in mind when you go. The schedule above is one published case from 2017, so do not assume it matches this year's schedule.

The best days to visit are the last two days with the parade and street dancing, and Tribal Day. For the exact schedule of the year, check the official announcements of the T'boli municipal office. For 2026 we found only individual events such as a mountain run on March 8 and could not find a full official schedule. Lake Holon is known to close for about two months from early January each year and reopen around the March festival (in 2025 it closed on January 4 and reopened in March), though dates vary by year, so if you want to trek the lake as well, check its entry rules separately. Rather than building a trip around the festival alone, it works well to combine it with nearby sights such as Lake Sebu and Lake Holon in a trip of about 2 nights and 3 days, so travel time is not wasted.

blocks.title: Twelve days with the founding anniversary

children.text: T'boli became a municipality on March 5, 1974, and the festival runs about 12 days from March 5 to mark the date. The long period puts the whole town in a festive mood.

On the first evening there was a torch parade along the national highway, followed by an opening salvo, concert and fireworks at the municipal plaza. The first night is when the most residents gather.
March 14 is listed as Tribal Day, with events showcasing T'boli culture and an evening concert recorded. It is the day when you can see tribal traditions most closely.
On the last morning, a grand parade and street dancing competition were held along the national highway. The colorful costumes and drumbeats make great photos.
The schedule included a pilgrimage to Lake Holon, which was named the cleanest inland body of water in the country in 2003 and 2004. Trekking and camping are possible there.
These include basketball, volleyball, shooting, motocross and off-road events, plus shows and pageants. The details change every year, so check the program for that year.

The town is reported to have a T'nalak weaving center, a museum and cultural village, and several waterfalls. Visit them in the gaps between festival events. For example, Hikong Bente is described as a 25-level waterfall, and "hikong" means waterfall in the T'boli language.

items.title: The last two days
items.subtitle: From the town to the parade

children.text: Go to the national highway in the town center and find a spot for the parade. In 2017 the grand parade began at 7:30 AM, but this varies by year.
Watch the street dancing competition. There is little shade, so bring a hat and water.
Eat lunch at a nearby restaurant and look around the town center.
Move to the municipal plaza or the cultural village to see tribal costumes and crafts.
Watch an evening concert or the closing program. If there are fireworks, watch them from the plaza.
Follow that year's official announcements for schedule and venues. The times above are examples based on the 2017 program.

items.title: Tribal Day
items.subtitle: Cultural events and a Lake Holon link

children.text: Check this year's Tribal Day schedule at the municipal office. In 2017 it was March 14 and began at 8 AM.
Watch events that showcase T'boli costumes, dance and brass ornaments.
After lunch, visit the T'nalak weaving center and the museum. Check opening hours locally.
Join the Tribal Day concert.
Trekking to Lake Holon may require a permit and a guide, so set aside a separate day.
There are flights from Manila (MNL) to General Santos International Airport (GES). Check the airline's notices for the timetable. You can also fly into Davao (DVO) and continue overland.
From General Santos, travel to T'boli via Koronadal. Check travel time and fares locally.

Take a van or jeepney bound for T'boli from the Koronadal public terminal. Vans marked 'Direct T'boli' run from the Marbel (Koronadal) terminal. Guides give about 45 minutes to 1 hour (based on 2012 and 2017 trips) or about 1.5–2 hours (2025), and a fare of ₱60 (2017 guide) versus ₱120~150 (2025 guide), so they disagree. Check locally.

For trips from the town to the highlands such as Lake Holon, guides describe registering and getting an orientation at the municipal tourism office and then taking a motorbike (skylab) taxi to the jump-off point.
Around town, the venues can be reached on foot, and for longer distances you take a tricycle or motorbike taxi. Fares vary with distance and bargaining.
Transport is crowded and lodging fills up early during the festival, so check transport and accommodation in advance.

The Seslong Festival is held every March, usually between March 5 and 16. Because the town's founding anniversary is March 5, the start date is fairly constant. Check the official announcements of the T'boli municipal office for that year's detailed schedule.

Weather in the highlands changes easily, so if you plan to head to areas such as Lake Holon, bring a rain jacket. The weather during the festival differs each year, so check the forecast before you leave.

There is not much lodging in T'boli itself, so during the festival it is hard to find a room unless you book in advance. As an alternative, you can stay in Koronadal, nearby Lake Sebu or General Santos and make a day trip. Check lodging availability and rates locally for that year. In town people often get around by motorbike taxi or tricycle, so it is convenient to book lodging close to the venues.

Eat at restaurants or the market in town, and stalls open around the festival venues. What will be open and how changes every year, so check locally. Carry plenty of cash and use bottled drinking water.

Before you go, check the official announcements or Facebook page of the T'boli municipal office for that year's schedule. The office phone is (083) 237 1205, and the office is reported to be open on weekdays from 8 AM to 5 PM.
Parades and street dancing are often held in the morning, so go early and find a spot.
The events take place on streets with little shade, so you need a hat, sunscreen and water.
Lodging is limited, so book several weeks before the festival or consider traveling from Koronadal or General Santos.
Ask politely for permission before photographing tribal events. Rituals are culture, not entertainment.
Carry cash in pesos. Many places do not accept cards.
Highland areas such as Lake Holon may require separate registration and a guide, so set aside a separate day.
Before or after the festival, visit Lake Sebu and the T'nalak weaving villages as well.

The schedule and venues of the Seslong Festival change every year, and in some years we could not directly confirm an official schedule. Be sure to check the latest announcement of the T'boli municipal office before you travel.

Some introductions mention traditional events such as horse fighting, but making animals fight is highly controversial and restricted under Philippine law. Do not go out of your way to seek out such events.
Transport and lodging are very crowded during the festival, so prepare in advance. On the last weekend in particular, roads in and out of town may be congested.
Security conditions can vary by area around South Cotabato, so check the latest advisories from your government and local announcements.
Mountain roads and weather change easily. Travel with a guide on highland itineraries.
Always ask permission before photographing tribal costumes and rituals.
A lake town near T'boli, known for T'boli weaving and brass craft. A good stop before or after the festival.

A lake in the crater of Mt. Melibengoy in T'boli, known to close for about two months from early January and reopen around the March festival (2025 example). Check entry and trekking rules separately.
The nearest large city, with an airport. You travel overland from there to T'boli.
Described as a place where you can see T'nalak, the traditional cloth woven by T'boli women. Check opening hours locally.
